answers.text: Power can be shared among governments at different levels. There is a general government for the entire country and governments at the provincial or regional level. In India we call them the Central or Union Government and the State Governments. The constitution clearly lays down the powers of the different levels of government, so power is divided between higher and lower levels. This is called federal division of power, and it is also called vertical division of power.

answers.text: In our country there is one government sitting in Delhi that looks after the whole nation, and every state like Kerala or Punjab has its own government too. Our constitution writes down exactly what each of them is allowed to do, and that is why power is split between the top level and the lower levels. Even villages have their own panchayat and towns have a municipality.

answers.text: There are two routes. In coming together federations, independent States come together on their own and pool their sovereignty to form a bigger unit, so the States usually have equal power, like the USA, Switzerland and Australia. In holding together federations, a large country decides to divide its power between the States and the national government, so the central government tends to be more powerful, as in India, Spain and Belgium.

answers.text: Communalism was seen as a major challenge to democracy, so the makers of our Constitution chose the model of a secular state. There is no official religion for the Indian state, and the Constitution does not give a special status to any religion. It gives all individuals the freedom to profess, practice and propagate any religion, or not to follow any, and it prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion.

answers.text: For comparing countries, income is considered one of the most important attributes, because more income means more of all things people need. Total income is not useful for comparison since countries have different populations, so we use average income, which is the total income of the country divided by its total population. It is also called per capita income.

Money acts as an intermediate in the exchange process, so it eliminates the need for double coincidence of wants. That is why money is called a medium of exchange.

answers.text: Alluvial soil covers the entire northern plains. It was deposited by the Indus, the Ganga and the Brahmaputra, and it is also found in the deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri. Alluvial soils are very fertile and contain potash, phosphoric acid and lime, which are ideal for sugarcane, paddy and wheat. Due to its high fertility, these regions are intensively cultivated and densely populated.

answers.text: Regulating and damming of rivers affects their natural flow, causing poor sediment flow and excessive sedimentation at the bottom of the reservoir. This results in rockier stream beds and poorer habitats for aquatic life. Dams also fragment rivers, making it difficult for aquatic fauna to migrate for spawning. Ironically, the dams built to control floods have triggered floods due to sedimentation in the reservoir.
